candidate.name: CORE-MATH cr_sincosf with x87 range and status model

positive_binary32_exhaustive.status_model_note: The numerical exhaustive sweep predated the status-model counter. The model was instead checked on the captured workload, curated boundary/classes, and the uniform-raw random run.
positive_binary32_exhaustive.note: Executed in bounded-memory exponent chunks; sine oddness and cosine evenness were not used to inflate the tested input count.

uniform_raw_random.note: The range guard retains all finite inputs with |x| >= 2^63. Mismatch density below that limit rises with exponent because native x87 uses finite-pi argument reduction.

conclusion.observed_gameplay_domain: CORE-MATH final binary32 outputs are exact for every captured key.
conclusion.bounded_domain: CORE-MATH final binary32 outputs are exhaustively exact for every positive binary32 value below 524288; the observed maximum angle is below 24.
conclusion.unbounded_domain: CORE-MATH alone is not a total replacement for arbitrary large finite angles. Corrections or a hardware-compatible reduction path are required beginning in exponent 146.
